answer: A thread snaps at its weakest link, so each strand must come from someone else. Every identity needs two holders outside its own knoll to supply and countersign strands, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct suppliers rather than one cooperative crew. Each strand is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A nebula audit replays a random strand each epoch, and an unconfirmed strand unravels the whole thread and forfeits its bonds.
